X-Robot LLM Index

What X-Robot is

- X-Robot is a finite state machine library for JavaScript and TypeScript.
- It is built for explicit state-driven logic instead of scattered booleans, ad hoc effects, and implicit async flow control.
- Core runtime imports come from `x-robot`; documentation, diagrams, serialization, SCXML, and code generation come from `x-robot/documentate`; structural validation comes from `x-robot/validate`.

Core mental model

- Define a machine with `machine()`.
- Define states with `state()` and move between them with `transition()` plus `invoke()`.
- Use `entry()` and `exit()` pulses for state work; pulses can be sync or async and can transition on success or failure.
- Use `guard()` for conditional transitions, `immediate()` for automatic transitions, and `nested()` or `parallel()` for composition.
- Context is frozen by default. Use `snapshot()` and history features when workflows need restoration or auditing.

Current docs map

- `README.md`: quick adoption overview and examples.
- `docs/overview.md`: documentation hub for guides, concepts, recipes, comparisons, and generated API reference.
- `docs/api/**`: generated API reference for exact exported modules, functions, types, and interfaces.
- `llms-guide.txt`: compact LLM-oriented guide for most coding and explanation tasks.
- `llms-full.txt`: full generated documentation bundle, including API reference, for broad or exact lookup.

Size and performance snapshot

- Current metrics are generated in `docs/performance.md`.
- The latest checked-in report lists X-Robot Core at 16.55KB minified and X-Robot with `documentate` plus `validate` at 79.93KB total.
- Covered benchmark scenarios report a 1.1x-15.1x speed advantage over XState.
- Treat these as repo-local benchmark outputs, not universal guarantees; use `docs/performance.md` for details and regeneration instructions.

Which LLM bundle to use

- Use `llms-guide.txt` when an agent needs the main concepts, public imports, practical examples, and enough context to implement typical changes quickly.
- Use `llms-full.txt` when an agent needs the complete docs corpus, generated API details, exact signatures, or cross-document lookup.
- Use this `llms.txt` file only as a short index and routing note.
